text.p: Pen pictures of the probable Bayern Munich team and the referee for Sunday's German first division clash with Borussia Dortmund:

Oliver Kahn. Goalkeeper. Age 27. Germany's second-choice keeper who is ambitious to make a career in the national team. Huge man at 1.88 metres who dominates the penalty area with both his stature and loud voice.

Lothar Matthaeus. Libero. Age 35. Germany's most capped player with 122 internationals and a former World Cup captain. His international days now look over and did not go to England with Euro 96 squad. He is slower than in his heyday but still a player who can turn a match with a piece of skill.
Markus Babbel. Defender. Age 24. Euro 96 player who was tipped to be Juergen Kohler's successor as main man-to-man marker in national team but who has yet to match the Dortmund player's consistency.
Samuel Kuffour. Defender. Age 20. Ghanaian international who came from Nuremberg this year and who has impressed the Bavarians.

Mario Basler. Midfielder. Age 27. Joined from Werder Bremen at start of season. The German international has promised a great deal in recent seasons but injuries have often hindered his progress. One of the country's most gifted players but his comments in public often get him into trouble.
Thomas Strunz. Midfielder. Age 28. Versatile German international who good player at the back but who can also go forward. Injuries have hindered his form in recent seasons.

Mehmet Scholl. Midfielder. Age 26. Attacking German international who known for his dribbling and ability to turn a game with a piece of remarkable skill. His often fiery personality can get him into trouble on and off the pitch.
Christian Nerlinger. Midfielder. Age 23. One of Bayern's rising stars who has been at the club since 1987 and who fits into the team well alongside the bigger names.
Markus Muench. Defender/midfielder. Age 24. Joined from Bayer Leverkusen at the start of the season. Operates on the left-hand side in absence of injured Christian Ziege.

Juergen Klinsmann. Forward. Age 32. Germany's captain and most well-known player has been heavily criticised this season for failing to score but ended his poor run last weekend. The former Tottenham player remains one of the most dangerous strikers in the game.

Alexander Zickler. Forward. Age 22. Former Dynamo Dresden player came under fire for his lack of sharpness in front of goal when he was thrown into the team because of injuries two seasons ago but has matured into a good partner for Klinsmann.
Lutz-Michael Froehlich. Age 39. Berlin referee who has been operating in the Bundesliga since 1989 and who is a FIFA referee since 1994.
